 Former PBA star Peter June Simon, 46, passes away
 November 20, 2026 
 FASTBREAK.COM.PH 
 Share this FASTBREAK story:
 Philippine basketball mourns the passing of Peter June Simon, one of the most prolific scorers in PBA history and a longtime cornerstone of the Purefoods-Magnolia franchise. He was 46.
 Simon reportedly suffered a heart attack while playing in a basketball game for players aged 40 and above in Davao City on Friday evening.
 Initial reports said the veteran guard suddenly collapsed during the game and was rushed by teammates to San Pedro Hospital, where medical personnel attempted to revive him. However, efforts to save his life were unsuccessful.
 Born on June 1, 1980, in Makilala, Cotabato, Simon rose from the basketball scene in Mindanao to become one of the most respected players in the professional ranks.
 His basketball journey began in Davao, where he collected three Most Valuable Player awards in collegiate competitions and earned the nickname “Sultan of Slams” after winning the distinction five times.
 He joined the Davao Eagles of the now-defunct Metropolitan Basketball Association in 2001, quickly becoming one of the team’s primary offensive weapons. His impressive performances, including a 41-point outing, earned him the MBA Discovery Player of the Year award.
 Simon also represented the Philippines in the William Jones Cup as a member of the MBA All-Stars.
 Following the MBA’s disbandment in 2002, he continued his development in the Philippine Basketball League, playing for Dazz Dishwashing Liquid, Hapee Toothpaste and Fash Liquid.
 His breakthrough in the PBL included a Second Mythical Team selection in the 2002-03 Challenge Cup and a championship with Hapee in the 2003 Sunkist Unity Cup, where he shared Finals Most Valuable Player honors with Rich Alvarez.
 He eventually captured the PBL Most Valuable Player award in the 2003-04 season, further strengthening his credentials before making the jump to the PBA.
 Although Sta. Lucia selected him 43rd overall in the 2001 PBA Draft, it was the Purefoods franchise that eventually gave him his professional opportunity, signing him as a rookie free agent in 2004.
 Simon initially played behind James Yap but gradually earned a bigger role through his scoring ability and consistency, eventually becoming one of the league’s most dangerous reserves.
 He remained a key contributor to the franchise’s success in the years that followed, helping Purefoods and its succeeding teams win multiple championships.
 One of the defining moments of his career came during the 2013-14 season, when he played an important role in the San Mig Coffee Mixers’ historic Grand Slam, winning all three conference championships.
 His contributions that season also earned him a place in the PBA Second Mythical Team and the PBA Press Corps’ Mr. Quality Minutes award.
 Over his 16-season career with the Purefoods-Magnolia franchise, he collected eight PBA championships alongside Yap and Marc Pingris, becoming one of the most recognizable figures in the team’s history.
 The organization eventually honored his contributions by retiring his jersey alongside Pingris during a halftime ceremony on December 25, 2021.
 Even after his PBA career, Simon remained active in basketball, continuing to compete and share his experience, including a stint with the Davao Occidental Tigers in the Maharlika Pilipinas Basketball League.
 From his humble beginnings in Mindanao to becoming a championship-winning PBA veteran, Simon leaves behind a legacy built on scoring brilliance, perseverance and years of service to Philippine basketball.
